items.title_translated_en: Wang Xingxing: Unitree Could Ship 10,000 to 20,000 Humanoid Robots This Year
items.summary_generated_en: Chinese humanoid robotics company Unitree expects to ship 10,000 to 20,000 units this year, according to its founder Wang Xingxing, who noted the global humanoid robot market remains in a hot phase after roughly three years of development. The company, which gained attention with performances on China's Spring Festival Gala, is expanding into commercial performances and aims to move into industrial and service applications.

items.title_translated_en: Robots Steal the Show at Spring Festival Gala, Netizens Lament Loss of Traditional and Human Touch
items.summary_generated_en: The 2026 China Central Television Spring Festival Gala featured an increased number of performances with humanoid robots from four tech companies, sparking mixed reactions online. While some viewers praised the displays as showcasing China's technological progress, others criticized the shift, lamenting a loss of traditional human charm and "New Year spirit" in the celebrations. The prominence of robots is seen as part of a strategic industry push, with reports indicating companies paid high fees for the exposure amid expectations of a wave of listings in the embodied AI sector.

items.title_translated_en: Sources: ByteDance's In-House Chip Team Exceeds 1,000, Plans Large-Scale Hiring.
items.summary_generated_en: ByteDance has expanded its in-house semiconductor development team to over 1,000 employees, with plans for large-scale hiring to advance its custom chip designs for AI and cloud computing, aiming to boost performance and cut costs. The company is reportedly progressing with projects like its SeedChip AI processor and considering the sale of its gaming subsidiary Moonton to focus resources on core areas like artificial intelligence.

items.title_translated_en: Sunac Faces Liquidation Hearing as Country Garden Nears Offshore Debt Restructuring by Year-End
items.summary_generated_en: Facing imminent liquidation proceedings, Chinese property giant Country Garden has reportedly agreed to key terms with its bank creditors and aims to complete its offshore debt restructuring by the end of December to avoid being wound up. The restructuring involves about $14.1 billion in debt, and the company has secured extensions from a Hong Kong court to allow time for the process, with a key hearing now set for August 11.
